text: 3137 Horky, with the provisional designation 1982 SM1, is a background asteroid from the inner regions of the asteroid belt, approximately 7 kilometers (4.3 miles) in diameter. It was discovered on 16 September 1982 by Czech astronomer Antonín Mrkos at the Kleť Observatory in the Czech Republic and is named for a hill near the Czech village of Horky. Horky is a non-family asteroid belonging to the main belt's background population. It orbits the Sun in the inner asteroid belt at a distance of 1.9–2.9 AU, completing one orbit every 3 years and 9 months (1,360 days) with a semi-major axis of 2.4 AU, an orbital eccentricity of 0.19, and an inclination of 2° relative to the ecliptic. The observation arc of Horky begins with a precovery taken at Palomar Observatory in November 1949, nearly 33 years before its official discovery. On 1 May 2019, it will pass 15 Eunomia at a distance of 1,440,000 km (0.0096 AU), and is also projected to make close approaches to 29 Amphitrite, 7 Iris, and 10 Hygiea. In the SMASS classification, Horky is a carbonaceous C-type asteroid, but data from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) indicate it is more likely a stony S-type. As of 2018, no rotational lightcurve has been obtained, and its rotation period, pole, and shape remain unknown. According to the NEOWISE mission survey, Horky measures 6.685 kilometers in diameter and has a surface albedo of 0.207, suggesting a stony rather than carbonaceous composition, with an absolute magnitude of 13.3. The asteroid was named after a hill and the nearby village of Horky in the Czech Republic, where Mrkos installed his first telescope in 1939, and the official naming citation was published by the Minor Planet Center on 29 November 1993 (M.P.C. 22828).
